title: Hitik sitao (Hitik pole sitao): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: Hitik sitao: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: Hitik sitao is a pole sitao variety. 45 to 50 days to harvest, 9.7 t/ha in trials. See its ratings and traits. Compare it with others.
excerpt: Hitik sitao is a pole sitao variety, also sold or known as Hitik pole sitao. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 2008 as NSIC 2008 PS 04. It takes 45 to 50 days from sowing to the first harvest, with 9.72 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

**Recommended for:** the areas in its trials, in both the wet and the dry season.

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Hitik sitao takes 45 to 50 days from sowing to the first harvest. That is about the average of the 7 pole sitao varieties with a day count, 45.4 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 9.72 t/ha trails the average of its group, 11.33. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing. Its seller gives first harvest about 45 days (dry season) to 50 days (wet season).

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in trials, rated under natural field conditions
rows: Took a middling share of damage

blocks.text: The pests and diseases that hit sitao fields most often: [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [bean fly](/pests/bean-fly), [cutworm](/pests/cutworm), [legume pod borer](/pests/legume-pod-borer). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Its pods grew about 42.4 cm long. The seed coat is brown.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Yield:** 10.5 t/ha dry season, 8.9 t/ha wet season in registration trials.
**Fruit:** Green pods about 42 cm, brown seeds.
Moderately tolerant to fusarium wilt, mosaic virus and pod borer.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: the registered pole sitao, the parent name of the newer Hitik #2, #3 and #4 lines registered in 2020. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Hitik sitao

It is recommended for both the wet and the dry season. Pole sitao climbs a trellis and bears for weeks, while bush sitao needs no trellis and comes in at once. Pick long, dark green pods that snap cleanly, and a variety rated against the bean fly and rust if you can. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

items.q: Is Hitik pole sitao the same as Hitik?
items.a: Yes. Hitik pole sitao is another name for Hitik, registered as NSIC 2008 PS 04. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes 45 to 50 days from sowing to the first harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 9.72 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Hitik?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
